answer:
The new commits fix the earlier divide-by-zero finding, but they add a new panic in `first`.

**Prior findings**
- `f-divide-by-zero` is fixed. `average` now returns 0 for an empty slice.
- `f-integer-division` was dropped, so I haven't raised it again.

**New issues**
- `first` panics when `n` is greater than `items.len()`. The neighbouring `last` clamps the same way with `saturating_sub`, so callers will expect `first` to be safe too.
- `average` sums into an `i32`. That overflows for large values, which panics in debug builds and wraps in release builds.

draftedFindings.title: `first` panics when n > items.len()
draftedFindings.body: `&items[..n]` panics with an out-of-range slice index if `n` is larger than the slice. The sibling `last` clamps with `saturating_sub`, so callers will reasonably expect `first` to be safe too. Clamp it with `&items[..n.min(items.len())]`.

draftedFindings.title: `average` sum can overflow i32
draftedFindings.body: `sum::<i32>()` panics in debug builds and wraps in release builds on large inputs. For example, `[i32::MAX, 1]` overflows. Accumulate in `i64` and convert back, which is safe because the average always fits in `i32`.
